question: Fed Rate Hike by September 2026 Meeting?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is increased at any point between December 16, 2025 and the completion of the listed Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting (inclusive of any rate hike announced as a result of the listed meeting). Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

If the listed meeting does not take place within 7 calendar days (ET) of its scheduled end date, 11:59 PM ET, and no qualifying rate hike has been announced, this market will resolve to "No".

Emergency rate hikes will qualify.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

# Fed rate hike by the September 2026 FOMC meeting: research notes (as of 2026-08-26)

## 1. Resolution source
- The Fed's open market page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm) would not load; the proxy refused the connection. I could not see its latest entry directly.
- 2026-07-29: The FOMC kept the target range at **3.50%-3.75%** by a 9-3 vote. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented because they wanted a 25bp hike. [Fed press release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm); [Atlanta Fed](https://www.atlantafed.org/news-and-events/2026/07/29/fomc-statement); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)
- The range has been 3.50%-3.75% since the late-2025 cuts. I could not find a primary Fed source confirming the exact December 2025 cut date.

## 2. Current status
- As of 2026-08-26, **no hike has happened** since 2025-12-16. The upper bound is still 3.75%. Whether this resolves Yes depends on the 2026-09-15/16 FOMC meeting or an emergency move before it. Nothing has settled the question yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-19: The July minutes said many officials thought a rate hike would probably be needed if inflation did not come down. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/fed-minutes-july-2026-officials-saw-need-for-rate-hike-if-inflation-doesnt-cool.html)
- 2026-08-12: July CPI came in line with forecasts: headline +0.1% m/m and 3.4% y/y, core +0.2% m/m. Reports say this made a September hike less likely. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/cpi-inflation-report-july-2026.html); [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/july-inflation-data-came-in-as-expected-lowering-the-odds-of-a-fed-hike-in-september-yet-again/); [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/economy/middle-road-july-cpi-likely-gives-fed-breathing-room-rate-hikes)
- Early August 2026: July payrolls reportedly fell by 23,000, well below estimates. That weakens the case for tightening. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/july-inflation-data-came-in-as-expected-lowering-the-odds-of-a-fed-hike-in-september-yet-again/)
- 2026-07-29: The July meeting was Chair Kevin Warsh's first. There were three hawkish dissents, and the 30-year Treasury yield rose above 5.2%, its highest since 2007. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html)
- July 2026: Waller said hot core inflation readings would lead the Fed to consider a near-term hike, though he also sees a credible path back to 2% without higher rates. Logan has called for "modestly higher interest rates." Hammack has said some number of hikes may be needed. [Mitrade/Motley Fool](https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1916977-20260720); [Newsquawk](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/primer---todays-fedspeak-includes-waller-hammack-goolsbee)
- Oil prices and Iran/Strait of Hormuz developments are cited as a key swing factor for inflation.

## 4. Base rates
- Since late 2025 the Fed has made no hikes. It held at every 2026 meeting through July: January (10-2, with two dovish dissents), March, April, June (12-0) and July (9-3, with three hawkish dissents). [Chatham](https://www.chathamfinancial.com/insights/fomc-recap-1-28-26); [Advisor Perspectives](https://advisorperspectives.com/dshort/updates/2026/06/18/feds-interest-rate-decision-june-17-2026)
- Three dissents in favor of a hike is unusual, and the Fed has historically often moved soon after a cluster of dissents. But under Powell and earlier chairs, the Fed rarely made its first hike of a cycle without first signaling it clearly.
- The Fed has not used an emergency intermeeting hike since the early 1990s. Emergency moves in recent decades have been cuts (2001, 2008, 2020).

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-12: CME FedWatch put the chance of a September hike at about 38%, down from about 48% the day before, with a hold at about 62%. Another source put the hike odds at 42%. The chance of a hike by December was about 45%. [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/12/july-inflation-data-came-in-as-expected-lowering-the-odds-of-a-fed-hike-in-september-yet-again/); [BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/575a7c94-fb73-4088-86dc-8bc15c88214b)
- After the July CPI report, Bank of America scaled back its call for three hikes by year-end.
- After the July meeting, futures were pricing two hikes, in September and December. [AgWest](https://www.agwestfc.com/education-and-resources/industry-and-economic-insights/economic-updates/updates-from-the-fed/fomc-meeting-results)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price for the September hike with a verifiable date between 2026-08-20 and 2026-08-26. In mid-to-late August, market pricing for a September hike looked to be in roughly the 25-40% range, but I could not pin down an exact figure as of 08-26.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Late August 2026: The Jackson Hole symposium, with a keynote by Chair Warsh. This is the main near-term signal for September, and markets are expected to react strongly to whatever he says about hikes. [Yahoo Finance live page](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/live/jackson-hole-fed-summit-live-kevin-warsh-keynote-speech-180442096.html)
- Late August 2026: July PCE inflation data.
- Early September 2026: The August jobs report. Another negative payroll print would argue against a hike.
- Mid-September 2026: August CPI and PPI, released shortly before the meeting.
- From about 2026-09-05: The pre-meeting blackout period starts, with no more Fed speeches.
- 2026-09-15/16: The FOMC meeting, with the statement, Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot, and Warsh's press conference.

I end slightly below the most recent market levels because I put extra weight on the status quo and on the Fed's habit of signaling a first hike well in advance.
